question_type: single weekly flow cell whose 'net' panel is OCR-truncated: date-window mapping + rebuild net as the sum of four component panels
decisive_step: Two decisions. (1) Map 'third Thursday .. fourth Wednesday of Jan 1939' to the reporting week that ends on that Wednesday: the table's weekly rows are Wednesdays (Jan. 4/11/18/25/Feb. 1 at treasury_bulletin_1939_04.txt:1188-1192), so Thu-Wed is exactly the 'Jan. 25' row (reference worklog Step 2, solution key_decisions 1). (2) Notice that in the OCR of the April 1939 table (treasury_bulletin_1939_04.txt:1178, title line 1174) the NET CAPITAL MOVEMENT panel keeps only three annual rows (1236-1239) and its weekly rows are gone, so the net for the Latin America column must be rebuilt as the sum of the four component panels' 'Jan. 25' cells (lines 1191, 1205, 1219, 1233) (reference worklog Step 4, verified as an identity on a complete issue in Step 6). No later issue reprints the week, so vintage is not a factor (worklog Step 8). All three pilot cells made both decisions.

a.path_summary: find_tables on the question nouns (a[6]) led to the Jan 1939 issue's copy of the table, which only runs to Oct 1938 (a[9]-[13]); a title-based find_tables (a[18]) listed the April 1939 issue with Jan rows. printings for the row/column (a[20]) listed the Jan. 25 cell of all four component panels in one issue. Raw sed of lines 1170-1265 (a[23]-[24]) showed the NET CAPITAL MOVEMENT panel truncated after its annual rows; two show_table attempts to find weekly net rows returned nothing (a[26], a[28]); a rg confirmed no net weekly rows in the Apr/May issues (a[30]-[32]). It then summed the four component cells with calc (a[35]) and answered with a 'net inflow' qualifier.

smallest_change.change: No change needed for this question: all three cells found the April 1939 table, mapped the Thu-Wed window to the 'Jan. 25' reporting week, saw that the net panel's weekly rows are missing from the OCR and rebuilt the net from the four component panels with calc, matching the reference.

alternatives.change: printings: print the row's section/panel label on every listed row and group the SUMMARY by (part, section, column, period) instead of (part, column, period) (otables.py printings_page, the `bycol` key). The model would then have seen four separate one-printing summaries, e.g. `  [1939-01-25] part1 'MOVEMENT IN SHORT-TERM BANKING FUNDS' col latinamerica: 1 printings, 1 distinct values - same in all printings`, instead of `4 printings, 4 distinct values - REVISED/DIFFERS across printings ... latest printing 1939_04 (...:1233)`, which invites a model following the 'take the latest printing' rule to pick the foreign-securities panel row alone.
alternatives.why_not_first: No cell was misled here (all read the panels from the raw table first), so it is a robustness fix for the hazard seen at a[20], b[16], c[20]; it would matter on a question where the model runs printings before show_table.

notes: (1) OCR defect: in treasury_bulletin_1939_04.txt the NET CAPITAL MOVEMENT panel (line 1236) keeps only three annual rows; the parser reports 51 of 60 rows. All three cells and the reference rebuilt the net from the component panels; only the reference verified the identity on a complete issue (worklog Step 6) and checked the weekly rows against the 'Total January' rows (Step 5). (2) printings hazard confirmed in source: otables.py printings_page groups its SUMMARY by (part, column, period) and never prints o['section'], so the four component panels of one issue appear as '4 distinct values - REVISED/DIFFERS across printings' with 'latest printing' = the last panel's row. Also a non-existent date in --row ('1939-Jan. 19') is silently widened to the whole month. (3) Page economics: show_table --long on this 14-column table pages at 7 rows (a[9]); --stitch with --cols 1,10,13 (b[8], c[9]) showed the whole relevant column for all panels in two pages, which is the efficient view for 'one column, many rows'. (4) Date-window mapping was done by reasoning in all cells (Thursdays/Wednesdays of Jan 1939); the reference used `cal`. A calc snippet (datetime) is available if the v10 text wants a rule for 'nth weekday' phrasing. (5) Answer strings with a unit/sign qualifier ('thousand dollars net inflow', 'inflow') were graded correct, so free-text qualifiers did not hurt here. (6) Cell b spent 312 s: one gate round for submitting before calc; the recompute_final rule fired correctly and did not alter the answer.
